newsitem.title: USA: Morris off on court ruling jitters--analysts.
newsitem.headline: Morris off on court ruling jitters--analysts.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc's share price dropped on Monday on further profit-taking triggered by a Florida court ruling last week, analysts said.
A Florida judge on Friday denied tobacco companies' motion to stop the State of Florida from suing the industry under state anti-racketeering laws.
Philip Morris dropped 2-3/8 on Friday and was off 2-1/8 at 109-3/8 in active trading at around midday today. Industry analysts cited followthrough selling from Friday.
Smith Barney analyst Martin Feldman, however, noted the stock had been up about $10 in the days prior to Friday's ruling and the stock's going ex-dividend on Thursday.
"I think the market is taking a little bit of a breather," Feldman said.
He said he did not think the Florida court ruling posed a "major threat" to Philip Morris.
He said he was putting a 12-month price target on the stock of $130.
